raw:
The retrieved literature is off-topic (wind turbines, rivers, food webs), so these hypotheses come from NAS-Bench-201 structure and prior knowledge of how the space behaves. Nothing was run against the benchmark.

Reasoning behind the groups:
- **Dead-edge masking.** If edge 0 or 1 is `none`, a downstream edit through node 1 or node 2 has little to act on, so conv upgrades there gain less.
- **Skip redundancy.** A parallel skip on edge 3 already provides a gradient path, so adding a conv elsewhere is worth less. A conv replacing `none` gains more when a skip exists, because the cell stays trainable.
- **Kernel complementarity.** Stacking 3x3 after a 3x3 on the deep chain saturates the receptive field, while a 3x3 after a pool or skip adds more.
- **Sibling pooling.** An avg_pool sibling dilutes the summation at a shared node, so a conv edit matters less there. A `none` sibling makes the edited edge the sole contributor, so it matters more.
